title: One of Us: experiences and challenges faced by staff members in german-speaking intensive care units caring for patients who are healthcare professionals themselves.
summary:
Healthcare professionals themselves can become seriously ill and require intensive care treatment. This creates a unique situation for the team: colleagues become patients. This can affect communication, decision-making, and the emotional strain on those involved – and raises questions about role clarity and equal treatment.
A few international studies have already provided insights into the related difficulties; however, data for the German speaking countries is currently lacking.
The “One of Us” study therefore examines how staff in German speaking intensive care units experience these situations, what challenges they perceive, and what support they need. 
The study is based on an anonymous online survey open to nurses, physicians, and other healthcare professionals working in intensive care units–including former intensive care staff. The questionnaire is based on an internationally established instrument. The findings will  contribute to a better understanding of how to professionally handle this unique care situation and to develop targeted support services for those affected.
conditions: Experiences of staff working in German-speaking intensive care units with patients who are themselves healthcare professionals.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Nurses, physicians and allied healthcare personnel practicing at the ICU
Exclusion criteria:
Trainees and interns are excluded, as they are still in the process of gaining qualifications and are not integrated into the team and care structures on a long-term basis.
